categories.main_business_segments: Viking Therapeutics operates as a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel therapies for metabolic and endocrine disorders. Its primary business segments are the research and development of drug candidates targeting obesity, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH/MASH), X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD), and muscle wasting conditions. The company’s lead programs include VK2735 (for obesity), VK2809 (for NASH/MASH), VK0214 (for X-ALD), and VK5211 (for muscle wasting).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Viking’s core technologies center on small molecule therapeutics, including dual agonists of GLP-1 and GIP receptors (VK2735), selective thyroid hormone receptor beta (TRß) agonists (VK2809 and VK0214), and selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs, such as VK5211). The company relies on advanced medicinal chemistry, receptor selectivity, and tissue targeting to optimize efficacy and safety. Manufacturing is outsourced to contract manufacturers under cGMP standards, and Viking does not operate its own production facilities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: As a clinical-stage company, Viking currently does not have commercial customers. Its intended end markets are healthcare providers and patients affected by obesity, metabolic liver diseases (NASH/MASH), rare neurological disorders (X-ALD), and muscle wasting following hip fracture. Upon approval, the company’s primary customers will be specialty physicians, hospitals, and potentially payors in the U.S. and international pharmaceutical markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Viking Therapeutics is headquartered in San Diego, California, and conducts clinical trials primarily in the United States, with some activities in Australia. The company holds global rights to its core assets and intends to pursue regulatory approvals and commercialization in major markets including the U.S., Europe, and other international regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Viking operates as a downstream player in the pharmaceutical supply chain, focusing on drug discovery, clinical development, and (future) commercialization. It outsources manufacturing of clinical and commercial supplies to third-party contract manufacturers and does not own or operate manufacturing facilities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on advancing first-in-class or best-in-class therapies for large unmet needs in metabolic and endocrine diseases. Key R&D initiatives include progressing VK2735 for obesity (both subcutaneous and oral formulations), VK2809 for NASH/MASH, and VK0214 for X-ALD, as well as exploring dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonists for obesity. Viking emphasizes innovation in receptor selectivity, tissue targeting, and combination therapies, and seeks to expand its pipeline through internal discovery and selective partnering.
categories.revenue_model: Viking currently generates no revenue, as it is a pre-commercial, clinical-stage company. Its future revenue model will be based on product sales of approved drugs, potential milestone and royalty payments from licensing or partnering agreements, and possibly out-licensing of non-core assets. The company may also pursue collaborations for commercialization in certain markets.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Viking faces competition from major pharmaceutical companies and biotechs developing therapies for obesity (e.g., Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, Boehringer Ingelheim), NASH/MASH (e.g., Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Gilead, Akero, Pfizer), and X-ALD (e.g., bluebird bio, Minoryx Therapeutics). In obesity, it competes with established GLP-1 agonists and emerging dual agonists. In NASH/MASH, it is positioned as a potential best-in-class oral TRß agonist. Viking is generally considered an innovative, high-potential challenger in its target indications.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, Viking had $902.6 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments, with an accumulated deficit of $487.9 million. The company reported a net loss of $110 million for 2024, reflecting increased R&D and G&A expenses as it advances multiple clinical programs. Viking has raised significant capital through public offerings and is well-funded to support operations through at least early 2026, with a growth trajectory tied to clinical progress and potential future commercialization.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Viking’s value proposition lies in its focus on highly selective, orally available, and potentially best-in-class therapies for large and underserved metabolic and endocrine markets. Its lead assets offer differentiated mechanisms (e.g., dual incretin agonism, liver-targeted TRß agonism) with promising efficacy and safety profiles in clinical trials. The company emphasizes broad metabolic benefits, combinability with existing therapies, and convenient dosing (oral and injectable), aiming to address significant unmet medical needs and improve patient outcomes.
